> Hushlog is basically a little box that measures really tiny voltages and saves them to an SD card. Most DIY data loggers just use the microcontroller's built-in ADC, which is fine until you try to measure something small like a thermocouple and it's all noise. So I'm using an actual 24-bit ADC (the ADS1220) with 4 input channels, plus a small OLED so you can see the readings live. I'm designing the whole board myself, including the RP2040 part from scratch instead of just slapping a Pico on it. The main thing I'm going for is making it quiet: separate power for the analog side, filters on every input, and keeping all the noisy digital stuff away from the ADC. Once it's built I'm going to short the inputs, measure the noise floor, and see how close I can get to the datasheet. Whatever number I get goes in the repo, even if it's bad lol

## Design

### 2026-10-02 — RP2040 core done — 5 hours, and it should boot

**5h**

RP2040 core done — 5 hours, and it should boot

Spent this whole sitting (~5h) drawing the brain of Hushlog: the RP2040 plus everything it needs to actually power up and run, before any of the logging hardware goes on. The RP2040 is fiddly because it doesn't run off a single voltage. It has a regulator built in, so you feed 3.3V into VREG_VIN, it puts out 1.1V at VREG_VOUT, and you have to loop that 1.1V back into DVDD yourself to power the core. Getting that wrong kills the chip, so that's where I was most careful.

Started by placing the chip and sorting the power pins. IOVDD, USB_VDD and ADC_AVDD all go to the 3.3V rail; VREG_VOUT ties back to DVDD as its own 1V1 rail.

![Screenshot 2026-10-02 155809](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/GBVzV6ZEx6TLZH5icrIze08E7bPrmQMk/c96ecc8d2bf51be0e71da77af11810d8672c13cc99e43e7b2f42e793f8d86ced.png)

Built out the full decoupling: a 100nF at every supply pin, a 10µF bulk cap on 3.3V, and 1µF + 100nF on the 1V1 core rail. Then the rest of the core — the W25Q128 QSPI flash (the RP2040 has no internal flash, it boots off this), the 12 MHz crystal with 15pF load caps, the USB-C connector with 5.1k CC resistors and 27Ω series resistors on the data lines, an AP2112K LDO making the 3.3V from USB 5V, and the BOOTSEL/RESET buttons plus an SWD header.

![Screenshot 2026-10-02 162245](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/GBVzV6ZEx6TLZH5icrIze08E7bPrmQMk/31ca8d3c493e406be16935504befb1102a4b83a53170adfddbddbb30940546f8.png)

Hit one snag with the flash: the SOIC-8 footprint I first assigned wasn't in my library, and ERC threw "footprint not found." Fixed it by opening the footprint chooser, clearing the filters (it was filtering for a footprint that didn't exist, so the list came up empty), and picking the standard Package_SO:SOIC-8_3.9x4.9mm_P1.27mm.

When I ran "Update Symbols from Library" it told me there was nothing to rescue, which is what you want — means my symbols are clean.

![Screenshot 2026-10-02 160644](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/GBVzV6ZEx6TLZH5icrIze08E7bPrmQMk/d15606733807dea8b2c705155e6bc3d724965565e10bb1c7408e4962a605064a.png)

The one check I really wanted to nail: I clicked the wire on pin 44 (VREG_VIN) to confirm it actually lands on +3.3V and isn't accidentally tied to the 1.1V rail. KiCad confirmed the net resolves to +3.3V.

![Screenshot 2026-10-02 163042](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/GBVzV6ZEx6TLZH5icrIze08E7bPrmQMk/ea246eeede6b841eb8ef7a174747013a929bc3439c6c351a5c01ae3df44b75e9.png)

Ran ERC to close out. 30 errors left, every one a GPIO "pin not connected." Those aren't bugs — they're my to-do list, one per pin waiting on a peripheral. I'm deliberately leaving them erroring instead of hiding them with no-connect flags; they'll clear as I wire up the ADC, SD card, OLED and screw terminals. The 34 warnings are all cosmetic library-version mismatches and don't affect the board.
